body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 16, 2026, and we’re starting the week with a warm one: expect a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. Overnight, a serious wrong-way crash on Highway 99 near 7th Standard Road claimed three lives, and firefighters battled a palm tree fire that spread to an apartment complex in southeast Bakersfield. Air quality is moderate at 97 AQI. Let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious incident unfolded around 12:44 a.m. on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road, where a wrong-way driver in a white Honda Accord collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado. The Accord caught fire after impact, and all three occupants inside died from their injuries. The BMW’s driver and one passenger sustained major injuries, while the two occupants in the Chevrolet escaped with minor injuries. Meanwhile, around 9:16 p.m., a palm tree fire spread to the roof of a two-story apartment complex at 6200 Spice Way off Villalobos Street. Engine 7 took incident command as additional units responded to the scene. Elsewhere, officers staged on a possible shooting at 128 Price Street that never materialized on the air, chased a DUI driver in a white BMW fleeing east from the 33rd Street area, and handled a long string of low-stakes domestics and disturbances, including a Camellia Village apartment where a wall was punched in. Shortly before 5:40 a.m., one vehicle struck a parked car at 11008 Myrtle Avenue, drawing multiple engine companies and Battalion 4 for patient assessment.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. It’s currently 91° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and no active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at 97 AQI. The week ahead will see a cooling trend as a Pacific trough brings “cooler” highs, ending the third Bakersfield heatwave of the season.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that three people are dead after a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99 early Sunday morning.** According to California Highway Patrol Bakersfield, a white Honda Accord was traveling northbound in the southbound lanes on Highway 99, north of 7th Standard Road, when it collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado, at around 12:44 a.m. The crash caused the Honda to catch fire. CHP says all 3 occupants inside the vehicle died from their injuries. The driver and one other occupant of the BMW sustained major injuries. The 2 occupants in the Chevrolet sustained minor injuries. Officials say it is unknown whether alcohol or drugs were a factor in the crash.

**KGET 17 tells us that a man was arrested in Bakersfield following a domestic violence standoff involving minors.** Bakersfield Police Department says the incident began as a domestic disturbance and escalated into a standoff with law enforcement. The arrest highlights the ongoing challenges of domestic violence in the community and the risks posed to children in such situations.

**According to 23ABC, Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs shared Fourth of July findings at a recent Friday meeting, revealing progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city.** Kevin Albertson, Chief of the Bakersfield Fire Department, noted that the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state, with injuries and fatalities reported up and down California. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains. Bakersfield City Councilman Eric Arias said stronger policies are in the works to deter illegal fireworks use.

## Something good

**23ABC shares a heartening story about Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, who traveled to San Diego to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community—a project he helped build from the ground up.** Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. The initiative aims to provide resources and support for individuals struggling with addiction, potentially improving the lives of many in the community.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several public meetings and events are on the calendar. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board convenes at 10:00 a.m. Later in the week, the Planning Commission meets on Thursday, August 20, at 5:30 p.m. Meanwhile, the Fox Theater has a busy lineup: Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los Caminantes, and Grupo Yndio perform on August 22; Rodney Carrington takes the stage on August 27; Cumbiatron: The Cumbia Rave follows on August 28; Willie Barcena performs on August 29; and Michael Return of the King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix also appears on August 29. Finally, the Mi Historia Tour Leyendas del Mariachi USA comes to the Fox on September 4. Be sure to check venues for details and times.
